title: Feature Garden — local model selector UX sketch
content:
Notes to self — feature garden / local model selector (rough)

Context and motivation:
- Problem: Customers building multi-model flows (e.g., fallback -> expensive high-fidelity -> cheap summarizer) struggle to express selection rules and to preview how routing affects latency/cost/quality tradeoffs.
- Current Redwood tooling exposes model catalog and runtime routing policies but it's hard to iterate on rules casually in the Console; needs a lightweight UX for composing + simulating selector rules against traffic samples.
- Goal: a small product increment called 'Feature Garden' — sandboxed composer where engineers can author model-selection logic, run quick simulations on sample logs or synthetic load, and push simple selectors as named policies to routes.

Assumptions:
- We can access anonymized sample traces or synthetic distributions for simulation (team: infra/observability to confirm data availability).
- Selector language should be intentionally opinionated and minimal (a handful of predicates + weights) to avoid becoming a full rule engine.
- First iteration targets hosted-api customers and internal engineers; later expand to Dedicated and Private.

What success looks like (early signals):
- 10 internal feature teams use the sandbox to prototype selectors in first 6 weeks.
- Average time-to-first-simulation < 15 minutes for a new selector.
- Selector preview shows clear delta in per-token cost and 95th latency estimate.

Rough user stories (priority order):
1) As a backend engineer, I want a drag-and-drop composer that lets me chain rules like "session.user_role == admin -> model-x" so I can prototype access-based routing.
   - Acceptance criteria: can create rule, name it, simulate against sample trace, and see which requests would be routed to which model.

2) As an ML infra engineer, I want to run quick cost/latency impact simulations given our recent traffic sample, so I can evaluate whether a new cheap model makes sense.
   - Acceptance criteria: show aggregate token counts, estimated cost delta, and estimated 95p latency change.

3) As a product engineer, I want to save a selector as a named policy and optionally tag it for canary rollout, so I can promote it to a route later.
   - Acceptance criteria: saved policy appears in policy list, has tags, and can be attached to a route in Console (manual step for initial launch).

4) As an SRE, I want quick safety checks (e.g., circular fallback detection, model capacity mismatch warnings) so we don't create policies that could overload small pools.
   - Acceptance criteria: warn on obvious capacity or incompatibility problems; block apply if fatal.

Feature sketch — UI flows:
- Entry: Console -> Model Routing -> "Feature Garden" (experimental badge)
- Composer panel (left): add predicates (user attributes, route path, prompt length, header flags, custom header), combine with boolean ops, set target model and fallback list, optionally set sampling weight.
- Simulation panel (right): sample input rows (choose dataset: last 24h sample / synthetic), run simulation -> results table with counts, example inputs, per-model token estimates, cost delta, latency estimate.
- Save / export: save policy (name + description + tags), run safe-checks, create a draft policy that can be applied to a route.

Selector primitives (proposal):
- Predicates: equals, in-set, regex, numeric comparison, percentile-based (e.g., top 10% prompt length), user_cohort tag.
- Actions: route_to(model), sample(p%), fallback(list), annotate(metadata)
- Weighting: ability to say route_to(modelA, 70%), route_to(modelB, 30%) for gradual traffic splitting in the sandbox (does not affect live routing until promoted).

Quick API sketch (for internal proto):
- POST /api/internal/selector/simulate
  body: {"policy": "...selector DSL...", "sample_id": "last-24h-1k"}
  response: {"results_csv_url": "...", "summary": "..."}

- POST /api/internal/selector/save
  body: {"name": "cheap-first-v1", "policy": "...", "tags": ["canary"], "owner": "leo"}

Open questions / decisions:
- DSL vs visual-only: do we surface a text DSL for power users? (lean: yes, show DSL toggled view)
- Where do we host sample traces? size & privacy concerns. Need SRE/observability sign-off.
- Safety model: what checks must block apply? (capacity mismatch, incompatible quantization, model not in customer catalog)
- Integration with Rollouts: for MVP keep promotion manual; roadmap: integrate with rollouts API for canary.

Mini experiments (short timeframe):
- 1-day prototype: implement lightweight client-side composer + fake simulation that runs against synthetic dataset (local) to get UX feedback.
- 2-week prototype: hook simulate API to real anonymized 1k trace and show cost/latency estimates computed by offline heuristics.

Dependencies:
- Observability: sample traces, anonymization pipeline (owner: Maya)
- Serving/runtime: API to get model token cost and latency profile (owner: Serving Runtime)
- Console: place for entry and list view (owner: Console Team)

Risks / mitigation:
- Risk: simulation estimates mismatch reality -> Mitigate: prominent disclaimer and conservative estimation (e.g., add uncertainty bands).
- Risk: team builds complex selectors that are fragile -> Mitigate: intentionally limit primitives in v1 and provide templates (e.g., "cost save", "latency-first").

Next steps (short):
- Sync with Maya and Samira: confirm sample trace access + anonymization approach (this week).
- Proto a toy composer in Figma + 30-min internal usability sync (by end of next week).
- Wireframe cost/latency estimation formula with Serving Runtime (quick math: per-token cost * token distribution; latency estimate from 95p per-token baseline + queueing fudge).

Notes-to-self:
- Keep the DSL small. No loops, no joins, just predicates -> actions.
- Think about a "policy playground" email invite list for internal beta.
- Remember to check GDPR/data residency concerns if any customer samples are used.

Random ideation parking lot (freeform):
- "Policy recipes" marketplace: simple premade selectors for common patterns.
- "Policy diff" view to compare two selectors and show delta in cost/latency and affected user segments.
- Export a selector as reproducible test harness input for CI: selector + sample -> replay test on deploy.

End of note — rough, messy, intentionally half-baked. Will iterate after talking to Maya/Samira and getting basic proto feedback.
